summary: Clarifies how explicit tracking works in Multicast VPN (MVPN), the procedure by which a multicast ingress node learns which egress nodes want a given flow. The base MVPN specifications (RFC 6513 and RFC 6514) were unclear in some scenarios. This document fills those gaps and defines a new way to handle wildcard routes. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: When a teacher sends a note to a class, it helps to know exactly who got it. This document makes the rules clear for how a network keeps track of who is listening to a group broadcast.

questions: what is explicit tracking in mvpn
what is a leaf a-d route
what is a wildcard s-pmsi a-d route
subtitle: How a multicast ingress router learns which egress routers want each flow, now with a single wildcard request.

tldr.problem: The base Multicast VPN specifications let an ingress node track which egress nodes want a flow, but they were unclear for wildcard routes, and tracking each flow under a wildcard needed one route per flow.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC clarifies the matching rules by adding a 'match for tracking', and defines a new LIR-pF flag so that one wildcard S-PMSI A-D route makes each egress node answer with a Leaf A-D route per flow.
tldr.outcome: An ingress node can track individual flows with a single message, at the cost of a possible burst of control-plane routes if the flag is set by mistake.

today: RFC 8534 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated. It updates RFC 6514, RFC 6625, RFC 7524, RFC 7582 and RFC 7900.

sections.title: The Problem with Wildcards and Tracking
sections.content:
In Multicast VPN (MVPN), an ingress node can ask to learn which egress nodes want a flow. This is called explicit tracking. It is requested by setting the LIR (Leaf Information Required) flag in the PMSI Tunnel attribute (PTA) of an S-PMSI A-D route. Each interested egress node answers with a Leaf A-D route.

RFC 6625 lets an S-PMSI A-D route carry wildcards in place of the source, the group, or both. If the ingress sets LIR on a (C-*,C-*) route, egress nodes answer with a Leaf A-D route carrying the wildcard. The ingress learns who is interested, but not which flows each egress node wants.

Tracking individual flows previously meant originating an S-PMSI A-D route for every flow. The RFC clarifies that case and adds a more efficient procedure. It also covers segmented P-tunnels, where the ingress cannot see past a segmentation domain boundary.
sections.eli5: Asking 'who wants anything?' only tells you who is in the room. To learn who wants which snack, you used to have to ask about every snack separately.

sections.title: The LIR-pF Flag
sections.content:
The RFC defines a new flag in the PTA Flags field, Leaf Information Required per Flow (LIR-pF). It may be set in the PTA of a (C-*,C-*), (C-*,C-G) or (C-S,C-*) S-PMSI A-D route, and in the PTA of a Leaf A-D route.

Support is OPTIONAL. The flag SHOULD NOT be set unless all the PE routers receiving the route are known to support it, so operators would typically guard it with a configuration knob. If LIR-pF is set on an S-PMSI A-D route, the originator MUST also set LIR. A receiver that sees LIR-pF without LIR MUST log it, then process the route as if both were set.

If some egress nodes do not support the flag, the ingress cannot learn the complete set of interested egress nodes, and some flows may look blackholed to those nodes. The ingress can detect this: a Leaf A-D route lacking a PTA, or with LIR-pF clear, in answer to a route with LIR-pF set reveals an unsupporting egress node. The ingress software MUST detect this and MUST be able to alert the operator.
sections.eli5: The new flag is a special 'tell me about each one' sticker. If some kids cannot read the sticker, the teacher will not get the full picture, so she should only use it when everyone understands it.

sections.title: Match for Tracking versus Match for Reception
sections.content:
RFC 6625 defines how a node finds the S-PMSI A-D route that is the match for reception of a flow. This RFC changes that rule: routes with no PTA, or whose PTA says 'no tunnel information present', MUST be ignored.

It then adds a match for tracking. For a flow, ignore any S-PMSI A-D route with no PTA, and any route whose PTA says 'no tunnel information present' with neither LIR nor LIR-pF set. Then apply the usual matching rules.

For example, suppose PE2 originates Route1, a (C-*,C-*) route whose PTA specifies a tunnel, and Route2, a (C-S1,C-G1) route with 'no tunnel information present' and LIR set. For (C-S1,C-G1), Route1 is the match for reception and Route2 is the match for tracking. The match for reception is never more specific than the match for tracking.
sections.eli5: One note tells you which road the flow travels on. A second note tells you whether anyone is counting travelers. They can be the same note or two different ones.

sections.title: Ingress Initiation and Egress Response
sections.content:
An ingress node has two ways to start tracking. In the first, it originates an S-PMSI A-D route for a specific flow with LIR set. The PTA may name a tunnel or say 'no tunnel information present'. In the second, usable only if the egress nodes are known to support LIR-pF, it sets LIR-pF in a wildcard S-PMSI A-D route, and egress nodes answer with a Leaf A-D route for each flow they need.

To stop tracking, the ingress withdraws a route that has no tunnel, or re-originates a route that has a tunnel without the flags.

On the egress side, if the match for tracking differs from the match for reception, the egress node MUST respond to both. When it responds to a match for tracking with LIR-pF set, it MUST originate a Leaf A-D route naming each flow, with LIR-pF set in the Leaf A-D route's PTA. The Route Distinguisher is copied from the S-PMSI A-D route, and the ingress PE address comes from its Originating Router field. If a wildcard route is the match for tracking of many flows, there is one Leaf A-D route per flow.

Leaf A-D routes MUST be withdrawn if the S-PMSI A-D route is withdrawn, if the egress node changes its Upstream Multicast Hop for the flow, or if it no longer needs the flow.
sections.eli5: The teacher can ask about one snack, or ask once about all of them. Each kid then replies for each snack they want, and takes the reply back if they change their mind.

sections.title: Tunnel Types, ABRs and ASBRs
sections.content:
For tunnel types listed in RFC 6514, the Leaf A-D route's PTA depends on the tunnel type. With Ingress Replication, it MAY also say Ingress Replication, with a non-zero MPLS label that the ingress then uses for that flow. It MAY instead use a zero label or 'no tunnel information present'. For any other of those tunnel types, the PTA MUST say 'no tunnel information present'. Other tunnel types need their own specification; without one, the egress node treats LIR-pF as clear.

When the egress node is an ABR or ASBR with segmented P-tunnels, a received PTA saying 'no tunnel information present' MUST be forwarded unchanged, including the LIR and LIR-pF flags. Leaf A-D routes coming back have their Route Target rewritten to the address from the Segmented P2MP Next-Hop Extended Community if present, otherwise from the Next-Hop field. This lets the ingress track egress PEs across domains, but only when the match for tracking differs from the match for reception.

On receipt of a Leaf A-D route that answers a wildcard S-PMSI A-D route it originated, the ingress MUST process it. With Ingress Replication and a non-zero label, it MUST use that label. Otherwise the information is for management and monitoring and does not change how traffic flows.
sections.eli5: Some roads need a special ticket number, and some do not. When a note passes through a border checkpoint, the guard must hand it on unchanged so the teacher still sees the same request.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 6513 and RFC 6514 apply. One new risk is that a single wildcard S-PMSI A-D route with LIR-pF set can draw a large number of Leaf A-D routes, so setting it by error or malfeasance can greatly increase control-plane overhead.

An ingress node that receives Leaf A-D routes with LIR-pF set in answer to a route with LIR-pF clear MUST log this by default. Implementations SHOULD have a knob to turn the logging off, since it can produce false positives. Withdrawing the route is not a good remedy, so the RFC advises relying on general control-plane protection.

IANA added an entry to the PMSI Tunnel Attribute Flags registry: value 2, name Leaf Information Required per-Flow (LIR-pF).
sections.eli5: If someone sticks the 'tell me everything' sticker on by accident, everyone starts sending long replies. The answer is to guard the mailroom well.
